about: What the sessions changed on the site, newest first, in plain words for the owner's Admin page ('What changed lately'). Add with: python3 check-tools/admin.py change "<what>". Nothing private: both repositories are public.

changes.what: Today's top 10s hub: 'Since last update' compares each market with its last trading day, so a weekend or holiday no longer shows 'no change' everywhere; 'days in the top 10' counts trading days (it had reached 28 on pages a week old)
Two untrue lines gone: the autopilot no longer says 'the AI model may sell early again' (those sales have been off since 17 Oct), and the AI chat says 25 markets have a daily top-10 page, not 24

The Admin page no longer asks you to check in for October's bill: it was $1.57, 7 cents over your $1.50, from two faults of 23-26 Oct that are already fixed; it says so and goes red again only if the bill climbs past $1.65. The daily cost check stopped counting known costs and a few cents of page refreshes as problems
Market figures: a new trade flashes within a second of a refresh, a row's price and % always flash the same colour, the figure changes a moment after the colour
Home page index cards: the name opens that index's daily top-10 page, Run screener runs the screener; both underline on hover; a new Russell 2000 daily page

Market figures flash like a broker's screen: only on a new trade, in the order trades happened, only the part that changed, a softer colour first then the figure; closed markets no longer flash on refresh; updates keep going 5 min while you watch without moving

Market panel figures were wrong for a few seconds on every page load (Bitcoin -0.83% for -0.09%, XRP up for down, Brent oil $117.64 for $113.43): its seven data functions now work the day's change out as the live updates do
Market figures on the home page, dashboard and daily pages now flash the moment the new price arrives (they waited up to 2.5 s); update_interval.sh tested on every kind of page
update_interval.sh works again: it shows and changes how often prices refresh (it had silently changed nothing since 18 Oct)
The daily update now waits 20 hours after the last one (it ran at 15:33 and again at 00:02)

Practice portfolio: the three cards read alike (value, today, since the start), in the order your account, same markets, S&P 500; under them one line each saying how far your account is ahead or behind, then cash and holdings; the coin note is gone
Two tests no longer reach the live sign-up and usage functions (one had registered a made-up trial account today)
The full check's re-check now re-runs the panel comparison and the header checks by themselves, without a 15-minute full run
The autopilot's Settings now say that two of every four shares are kept up to 20 days (the longer-holds trial), and the full check's panel comparison allows for it
The autopilot tab's 'Needs you' no longer says the cash is too low while its budget is automatic: all its money is invested and it buys again when a holding is sold
Sector funds line now says which 3 funds it holds right now (Chips, Energy, Technology) and that the others, gold included, are only bought when in the top 3

Coins: the autopilot never buys them when it chooses the markets (Manual users can still tick them); the S&P card now says where the account stands without the old coin trades; the By market list shows results in dollars only, without the confusing Total bought column

The second card is now If all in the S&P 500 instead; the third card loads with the others on a refresh (the index prices come with the holdings' prices: 6 requests instead of 32); the Admin page splits the gap to the S&P 500 into choosing shares and choosing markets

By market list: the S&P 500 lines taken out (the second card already has it); your own buys get their own row; the third card shows its own today figure like the other two, and the day figures sit neatly under each total

By market list: the last column now shows what each market's own index made with the same money (up or down, like your result beside it), not the difference; the third card is now called Same markets, no AI

The practice graph's gold line now compares each market with its own index (the Hang Seng's buys with the Hang Seng, and so on), not the S&P 500; a third card at the top, If in their own markets instead, gives the same figure; the S&P card says how much it is down since the start

Practice portfolio top: two figures side by side, your account and what the same $100,000 would be in an S&P 500 fund, each with its day's move beside it and how much higher or lower the account is; the separate Today box is gone

By market now compares each market with its own index (Dow 30 buys against the Dow, NASDAQ 100 against the NASDAQ 100); All markets adds those up. The S&P 500 stays as a small grey line, the top card and the graph's gold line
By market, All markets: the autopilot's line now gives its dollars against the S&P 500 (▼ $1,326) and says its percent is per dollar traded, so it no longer looks at odds with the 0.9% beside it

The daily update can no longer run twice in a day after a restart: its once-a-day lock was in a folder macOS empties on restart (30 Oct: a restart at 3:04 pm, a second run at 3:33 pm). The daily Claude review had the same fault. A second run, if ever started by hand, now says so in its email
Today's top 10s page: from the next daily update, each market shows its change since the day before (▲/▼, and a 'new' leader), and the Updated date stands out
A new trial for profit: half of new share buys are kept up to 20 days instead of 5 (the replay's clearest finding), beside the current rule; decided at 30 finished trades each way
The chat knows the free trial includes the AI autopilot; the autopilot tab explains 'Holding 46' when its number is lower; no past sell dates
Stock analysis guide fits a phone (two boxes side by side were wider than the screen); found by the deploy's own phone check
Home page pricing: a button on each plan (Start free trial, or Choose Starter / Pro / Elite when signed in)
Google Analytics now counts sign-ups, analyses, the autopilot switched on, checkouts and payments; four pages had no analytics; a thank-you notice after paying
Admin page: 'Done in the last 3 days' above 'Coming up'
By market, All markets: a line with the autopilot's holdings against the S&P 500 and against their own indexes, on the same holdings
Practice portfolio: the third figure is now 'Against the S&P 500: ▼ $… behind' (the fund's own value in the small print); every big number is about your account
This week in the markets (home page): each announcement's market now links to that market's top 10 today, and its figures read 'expected … · last time …'
Two trials decided and kept: the pages' market data once a minute (Lambda calls down from about 15,000 to under 2,500 a day) and the daily review by Claude
The weekly review of the autopilot (30 Oct): no faults; no rule change, as no group of 30 trades is clearly up or down; Claude's forecast lowered from 25% to 20%
The daily email now names a step the system stopped (out of memory) and warns when news.html grows too large; the 27-29 Oct emails had missed it
Market news articles get their 'Read full article' link again (it had come out blank since the script was written, on the news page and the home page's list)

The daily update had stalled: news.html had doubled itself to 5.8 GB since 27 Oct (a fault in the 26 Oct news fix), so today's run hung 8 hours and uploaded nothing. Fixed the cause, added a guard, restored the page, and the run then finished. The daily email now says when a step is killed.
The search's news box shows only when a suggestion is picked, so the suggestion list is never hidden
The home page's search boxes show a share's latest 3 news headlines and a link to its page when it is picked (or its code typed)
Your own buys and AI autopilot on the graph each draw the gold S&P 500 line too (the same money in the fund on the same days), so every view compares with the S&P the same way
The graph's measured stretch shows while you hold and clears when you let go, as broker apps do
On the graph, a chosen market's line is called the autopilot's buys from that screener, so it cannot be mistaken for the S&P 500 fund's line
Click and drag across the practice graph (a finger on a phone) shows the change between the two moments, for the account or the market chosen and for the S&P 500 fund over the same stretch
The By market list on the graph opens on the market you chose, not at its top
The S&P 500 card on the Practice portfolio shows the fund's own day (Today, or Last trading day while the US market is shut), to set beside the account's Today
Website deploys clear the cache once, not file by file: that cost $0.39 on 25 Oct after the month's 1,000 free paths ran out; the daily cost check now counts them
Stock news reaches the news page again (it stopped on 24 Oct when the shared footer went in); the site check now watches it
Plan cards now tick only what exists, with alerts, white-label and the other planned features marked 'Coming soon'; signed-in members get a 'Choose a plan' button in the home page's pricing
The Admin page now says who does each thing in 'Coming up' (you with Claude, your Mac, or AWS by itself), lists the next daily update, and shows the last three daily updates with a tick or a warning
The 'Do you need to check in?' card no longer turns amber for proposals the next session builds anyway; it does if one waits over a week
The notes that guide each session are now one of the site's parts, and tidying them (out of date, said twice, expired temporary notes) is part of every weekly review
AWS cost is now checked every day for free: a service's spend jumping, a database table or Lambda calls spiking, the month over your $1 target or $1.50 limit; anything found goes in the daily email

Found most of the AWS database bill: the daily report clean-up read the whole report table 64 times a day (once per account) and applied one account's setting to everyone's reports. It now reads only that account's reports: about $0.50 a month saved, and no account's reports are hidden by another's setting
The daily email now says 'Nothing needs you' or lists exactly what failed (with the error line), then what the run did; the day's log is kept so a session can read it without you copying anything
The daily site check now warns when the news stops updating (newest article over 2 days old), and the daily email names it

Every website deploy now runs the site's checks on the changed pages before anything is uploaded (a shared file: ten kinds of page), and stops if the change breaks something; until today a deploy only checked it was the tested file

The menu now stands in the same place on every page: on the sign-up page it sat 31px left of the others (a hidden placeholder took room), on the unsubscribe page 31px right for signed-in visitors (no bell). The header check now compares every page
